doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The All in Love Is Fair billboard on Sunset
summary: She cannot remember seeing the huge Sunset Boulevard billboard.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: In 1974 you had an album called All in Love is Fair and a huge billboard on Sunset Boulevard.
I don’t know. I might have.
I was going to ask you what it felt like to drive down Sunset Boulevard and see you larger than life.

I don’t know. I swear I don’t remember. You know, when you’ve lived a life as full as mine, and as long, and done as much as I have, it is very difficult to isolate and remember things, bring up – one of these days, maybe I’ll be able to get it together, but right now I can’t remember. I’m glad you told me that. That’s nice to know.
There’s a picture of it in John Levy’s biography.
Well I saw it and just didn’t pay any attention.
At Lark at Arnold. And Larkin Arnold
Oh God, Lark and Arnold Larkin Arnold, Capitol Records.
